chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, wishful thinking (daydreaming) is the work of undue concern (whispering), and the most frequent trap of Satan is eating clay; and it bequeaths illness to the body and stirs up disease. And whoever eats clay, so he becomes weaker than the strength he had before he ate it, and weaker than the action he was doing before he ate it, he will be held accountable for what is between his strength and his weakness, and will be punished for it.

key_terms.أَكْلُ الطِّين: Eating clay (metaphor for a specific spiritual/physical state)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical consequence of excessive wishful thinking (tamanni) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) identifies *al-tamanni* (wishful thinking or idle dreaming) as a subtle form of *waswasa* (Satanic whispering) that paralyzes spiritual and physical vitality. Using the metaphor of 'eating clay,' he illustrates how this state causes a person to lose their strength and capacity for action, resulting in divine accountability for the potential deeds they failed to perform due to this lethargy.
